tasks.notes: Scope/cost of leg (d) inside the exam. The Proof assigns leg (d) to the second `Run:` ("the bridge case passes — the second `Run:` is red if any one of them lacks the sentinel"), and the pytest bridge (tests/test_fleet_suite.py:62) already auto-discovers each of `test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_effort.mjs` and `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs` as its own case. `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_render_env.mjs` nonetheless re-runs all three as subprocesses (SIBLING_SIMS / `sim()`), and one of them — `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs` — itself spawns `test_sandbox_boot.mjs` and `test_sandbox_boot_approval_evidence.mjs` (test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs:278-279), so the new exam nests two levels deep and roughly duplicates the boot-sim work of the family on every suite run — far more than the "few boots, started concurrently through bootAsync" the third GLOBAL CONSTRAINT describes. That constraint carries no `Check:` the driver ran, and the evidence that bears on it is green (the exam is 35 s wall, `pytest -k sandbox_boot` exit 0 in 257 s, all well under MJS_TIMEOUT=300), so this is advisory only: the legs (a)/(a2)/(b)/(c) that the exam alone can establish are intact. If the duplication is not wanted, dropping the SIBLING_SIMS spawns and the leg (d) loop (lines with `sim()`, `siblings`, and the `for (const file of SIBLING_SIMS)` test block) leaves M3's sentinel clause resting on the pytest `Run:`, exactly where the Proof puts it; `SIBLING_SIMS` would then need to stay only as the leg (c) sweep's coverage list.; Comment overstates what leg (a2) waits for. `test_sandbox_boot_render_env.mjs` leg (a2) awaits `bareBoot()` and `plantedBoot()` before calling the blocking `boot()`, with the comment "rather than holding the event loop while its siblings are still draining their pipes" — but the three sibling sims spawned at module load are still live at that point, and `spawnSync` blocks the event loop, so their stdout/stderr pipes really do go undrained for the duration of that boot. It is harmless in practice (each sim prints a few KB, far under the 64 KB pipe buffer, and the blocking boot returns in ~0.7 s per the exam evidence), so nothing fails; the comment just claims a property the code does not have. Either reword it to say only the two promised boots are awaited, or await the `siblings` promises too before the synchronous boot.; Cost of leg (d): `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_render_env.mjs` spawns three complete boot sims in-process (`test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_effort.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs`, lines 255-286 of the new file). Each is already its own pytest bridge case, and `test_sandbox_boot.mjs` is listed in `SLOW_FIRST` in `tests/test_fleet_suite.py` as one of the longest poles; nesting them makes the new exam's wall equal to the slowest of them plus its own three boots (the EXAM EVIDENCE shows the leg alone at 34,070 ms of a 35 s run) and runs that pole twice per suite. Global constraint 3 asks that "a new exam adds at most a few boots, started concurrently through `bootAsync`, never a serial chain of them" — this exam adds three of its own boots (compliant: two through `bootAsync`, the blocking one after they land) plus roughly a whole boot suite's worth through the spawns. The constraint carries no `Check:` command, so this is my reading of prose and blocks nothing, and the driver's `python3 -m pytest tests/test_fleet_suite.py -k "sandbox_boot" -q` came back exit 0 (257 s, 12 passed), so it is not failing today; the exposure is the `MJS_TIMEOUT = 300` cap under a full `-n auto` run, where the nested pole competes with its own bridge case. The Proof already assigns leg (d) to a `Run:` rather than to the exam — "the second `Run:` is red if any one of them lacks the sentinel [M3]" — so dropping the three `spawn`s and the `SIBLING_SIMS` loop (keeping `SIBLING_SIMS` only as leg (c)'s sweep-coverage list, which it already serves at line 409) would leave M3 established by the same evidence at a fraction of the wall. If the nested runs are kept deliberately, that is defensible — the redundancy is what makes the exam self-contained — but it should be a conscious choice, not an accident.

The mechanism is fully pinned here — `<ctx.home>/systemd-run.env` shows one `FLEET_RENDER_ENV=` line and it is `renderEnvPath(ctx)`, so the script's `${FLEET_RENDER_ENV:-…}` fallback at `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:72` is never reached — but the plan's own live reading (Context: "the baseline is green again on a plugin-target run with `render` set is a live fact for the PR body, not a `Run:` here") is the part this environment cannot present.

completenessFindings.detail: Task 1, Proof leg (d) / global constraint 3 ("a new exam adds at most a few boots"): `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_render_env.mjs:198-229,367-376` implements leg (d) by spawning three whole sibling sims as child processes (`test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_effort.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot_state_exams.mjs`), rather than leaning on the second `Run:` (`pytest -k sandbox_boot`) that the Proof names as leg (d)'s check. Beyond its own three boots this charges dozens of nested boots to a single bridge case, and `tests/test_fleet_suite.py:5-22` records that exact shape as a scheduling defect already removed once: "test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs leads it as the longest sim that boots fleet/sandbox-boot.sh — the pole test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs used to hide. The merge sim ran it and six other boot siblings inside itself and no longer does." The new exam re-creates that hiding — it nests `test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, itself a `SLOW_FIRST` pole, while not being in `SLOW_FIRST`, so under `--dist load` it is dispatched in relative-path order carrying a wall at least as long as the pole it contains. Not blocking: the driver's own runs are green and inside the 300 s `MJS_TIMEOUT` (`pytest tests/test_fleet_suite.py -k sandbox_boot -q` exit 0, 12 passed in 250.40 s; `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_render_env.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED'` exit 0), and the sims are spawned concurrently, not as a serial chain. The Claim itself (M1/M2) is proven by legs (a)/(a2)/(b), which need none of this nesting.
